skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Search the web and extract page content through the inference.sh belt CLI using Tavily and Exa apps. It supports search answers, URL extraction, source gathering, and research workflows for agents and RAG.
skill.summary: Run Tavily and Exa web search or extraction workflows through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly Markdown code spans, fenced command examples, and documentation links rather than Ruby backtick execution. I found no prompt injection text in SKILL.md, but the skill grants broad Bash(belt *) access and sends user inputs to remote services. Tighten allowed tool scope and add clear privacy and command-quoting guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact belt app run commands needed for Tavily and Exa, or split broad platform access into a separate skill.
Show safer invocation patterns that avoid shell interpolation, such as using input files or a documented escaping step for user queries and URLs.
Warn users that searches, URLs, and extracted content are sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, or model providers.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Command Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools: Bash(belt *), which permits any belt subcommand instead of only the documented Tavily and Exa app runs. A prompt injection or mistaken instruction could run other belt workflows under the user account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 4 explicitly grants a wildcard belt command permission, and the skill later documents multiple remote app runs. The risk is scoped to belt, but the permission is broader than the advertised search and extraction use case.

semantic_findings.title: Inline Bash JSON Input Can Enable Injection
semantic_findings.description: Several examples place JSON inputs directly inside single-quoted Bash commands. If a user query or URL contains a quote or shell metacharacter, an agent could compose an unsafe command string.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file provides command templates with inline single-quoted JSON and user-controlled query or URL fields. There is no wrapper or escaping guidance shown, although actual exploitation depends on how the agent builds the command.

content.value_statement: Current web research often requires separate tools for search, extraction, and summarization. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable Tavily and Exa commands through the inference.sh CLI.
actual_capabilities: Runs Tavily search-assistant queries through the belt CLI.
Extracts clean text and images from public URLs with tavily/extract.
Runs Exa search, answer, and extract apps through inference.sh.
Shows workflows that combine search results with Claude model calls.
Provides documentation links for agent search and research workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends queries, URLs, and extracted content to remote services.
Results depend on Tavily, Exa, source availability, and provider limits.
Does not provide interactive browser automation or authenticated site scraping.

use_cases.title: Gather Source-Backed Research
use_cases.description: Search public web sources and collect links, snippets, and answer summaries for a research question.

use_cases.title: Prepare RAG Inputs
use_cases.description: Extract readable text from public URLs before passing the content into retrieval or summarization workflows.

use_cases.title: Check Claims Against Current Sources
use_cases.description: Use search and answer tools to compare a claim with recent public sources and supporting links.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for [topic]. Return a concise answer, the strongest source links, and any date-sensitive caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Public Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract readable content from these public URLs: [URLs]. Summarize each page and preserve source titles.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Search Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Tavily or Exa to compare [option A] and [option B]. Include source quality notes and unresolved questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the best sources, and prepare a source-grounded brief for [audience]. Separate facts, uncertainty, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Search for best practices for building AI agents.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with ranked source links, recurring recommendations, and notes on which sources are strongest.

output_examples.input: Extract two public article URLs and summarize each one.
output: Article one: title, clean text summary, key claims, and source URL.
Article two: title, clean text summary, key claims, and source URL.

output_examples.input: Answer a factual question that needs a current source.
output_examples.output: A direct answer with supporting source links and a short note when source dates affect confidence.

best_practices: Review source URLs before relying on extracted or summarized content.
Use specific search questions and date constraints when freshness matters.
Avoid sending secrets, private URLs, or confidential text to remote search tools.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated answers as verified facts without checking sources.
Do not extract private or access-controlled pages without permission.
Do not paste tokens, credentials, or confidential documents into search inputs.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Tavily and Exa apps through the inference.sh belt CLI.

faq.question: Does this skill require setup?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the belt CLI, a login, and access to the required inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Can it browse websites directly?
faq.answer: No. It calls search and extraction APIs through belt instead of controlling a browser.

faq.question: Can it return source links?
faq.answer: Yes. The search apps can return answer summaries with source links when providers supply them.

faq.question: Is it useful for RAG workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can gather public web text before retrieval, summarization, or answer generation.

faq.question: What privacy limits should users know?
faq.answer: Searches, URLs, and extracted content may leave the local environment and reach remote providers.
